title: Completed open endpoint comparisons transport normalized derived limits
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a Noetherian adic datum with finite perfect quotients $P_n=A/I^n$, completed coefficient sheaves $A_V=\lim_n(P_n)_V$ and strict reduction towers [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow T,j':U'\hookrightarrow T',u:T'\to T,v:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open square with $j$ quasi-compact [def-cbc-open-immersion-square, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use exact ringed extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$ be intrinsically derived $I$-complete, with $j_!K$ complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Use its canonical quotient/open comparison $(j_!K)_\bullet\simeq J_jK_\bullet$. Set
$$Q=Lu^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(j_!K)_\bullet,\quad C=Lv^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet,\quad M=r_UK_\bullet,\quad H=G_vM,\quad N=G_uJ_jM,$$
where pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], $r_V$ is restriction along $\underline A_V\to A_V$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and constant-$A$ operations are [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Fix the canonical scalar/finite-reduction comparisons $a:r_{T'}Q\simeq N$, $d:r_{U'}C\simeq H$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Write $e:r_{T'}J_{j'}\simeq J_{j'}r_{U'}$ for the identity-of-extension-presheaves comparison of [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-limit-coherence] for the ring map $\underline A_{T'}\to A_{T'}$, and $b=J_{j'}(d)e_C$.
Write $\widehat L_V$ and $L_V$ for completed-ring and constant-$A$ total derived inverse limit respectively. For scalar restriction and the two coefficient versions of $j'_!$, use exactly the normalized comparison $\lambda_F:FL\simeq LF^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], including its strict-augmentation normalization, as specified for these four functors in [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-limit-coherence]. These open comparisons are isomorphisms, with $j'$ quasi-compact by base change [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. The canonical source endpoint is
$$\widehat a=L_{T'}(a)\lambda_{r_{T'},Q}:r_{T'}\widehat L_{T'}Q\simeq L_{T'}N.$$
The canonical target endpoint is
$$\widehat b=j'_!\bigl(L_{U'}(d)\lambda_{r_{U'},C}\bigr)e_{\widehat L_{U'}C}:r_{T'}j'_!\widehat L_{U'}C\simeq j'_!L_{U'}H.$$
They agree with the finite-reduction and completed-pullback endpoint comparisons, carrying the quotient-tower completion units to the constant-$A$ units. They satisfy the endpoint pasting identity
$$\widehat b\circ r_{T'}((\lambda^{\mathrm{comp}}_{j',C})^{-1})=\lambda_{j',H}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(b)\circ\lambda_{r_{T'},J_{j'}C}.$$
Consequently, for every derived strict-tower morphism $\theta:Q\to J_{j'}C$, define $B_\theta=(\lambda^{\mathrm{comp}}_{j',C})^{-1}\circ\widehat L_{T'}(\theta)$. In the stated endpoints its scalar restriction is
$$\widehat b\circ r_{T'}(B_\theta)\circ\widehat a^{-1}=\lambda_{j',H}^{-1}\circ L_{T'}(b\circ r_{T'}(\theta)\circ a^{-1}).$$
These identities are natural in the coefficient complex and the strict-tower morphism. They impose no open-unit-mate condition on $\theta$, no etale-origin or common degree bound, and no faithfulness condition on derived evaluation.

proof.text: Use the pro-etale slice presentation of each open extension and the invertible localized open unit to prove both ordinary open extensions fully faithful. The ringed scalar/open comparison places the scalar-restricted completed extension in the essential image of the constant extension, making its counit invertible there. The explicit inverse-mate formula is a composite of this counit, the invertible completed open unit, and the specified scalar/pullback isomorphism. Thus the specified scalar/open mate is invertible, including on the empty open.

proof.text: Prove that exact localization preserves invertibility of the open adjunction unit: on a complex the unit is the localized degreewise unit conjugated by exact-functor factorization isomorphisms, and essential surjectivity extends this to every derived object. Apply this both to modules and to strict towers. Transport the ringed strict reduction isomorphism through canonical left-adjoint isomorphisms to the endpoint open extension; it puts reduction of an extended object in the essential image of strict open extension. Its counit is therefore invertible there. The explicit inverse-mate formula gives invertibility of the specified reduction transpose. Naturality is the naturality of that inverse mate.

proof.text: For any endpoint limit mate, the unit equation for mates and naturality of the constant-diagram comparison prove strict-augmentation normalization. Construct the normalized Roos comparison using the recorded cornerData and comparisonData. Conjugate its equation by the canonical Roos-to-limit isomorphisms on complexes; their projection equations identify the resulting map with the ordinary preserved-limit comparison. Its cochain right-derived unit equation is ExchangeDerivedPushNormalized. The uniqueness theorem exactDerivedMate_eq therefore identifies that invertible comparison with cbcEndpointLimitMap. Scalar restriction preserves products; transfer open-extension product preservation through the pro-etale slice equivalence. Apply this argument to the scalar functor and to both coefficient versions of the open extension.

proof.text: Apply the exact derived cube theorem to the ordinary scalar/open square and its four identity-component constant-diagram squares. Its ordinary cube is checked componentwise. The exchange-mate cube under the four constant/limit adjunctions gives the normalized scalar/open limit square. Cancel its invertible factors to obtain the inverse square.

proof.text: Compare the exact-localization adjunction with the right-derived adjunction transported through rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Both units have the same cochain factorization, hence localization extensionality and Adjunction.ext identify them. The ordinary constant/open unit square is componentwise the open unit. Localize it with mate_unit_Q to obtain the specified derived constant/open unit square. Transpose the requested reduction augmentation equation. Naturality of the quotient augmentation, its pullback compatibility reduction_augmentation, and the derived constant/open unit square give equality. Cancel the inverse reduction isomorphism.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of the base-changed open follows from its pullback presentation. Compose the inverse scalar/open limit square with the target finite-reduction map and use naturality of the constant open limit isomorphism; this gives the endpoint pasting identity. For any strict derived tower arrow theta, use scalar-limit naturality, the pasting identity, and cancellation of the source endpoint isomorphism to obtain the stated conjugation formula. These are equalities in the derived category of strict towers and use no faithfulness of evaluation.
